title.description: The problem's name, as it would appear at the top of a page.

topic.description: The technique the problem is really about: two pointers, monotonic stack, topological sort.

statement.description: The problem, stated the way an interviewer would write it on a shared doc. Plain prose, no markdown headings.

constraints.description: The bounds, one per line, as they would appear under CONSTRAINTS.

starterPython.description: A COMPLETE runnable Python 3 program. It must read the test input from standard input in exactly the format of `stdinFormat`, call the candidate's solution, and print only the answer. Leave the solution body as a clearly marked stub the candidate fills in. It must run without error before they touch it, printing nothing useful.

starterJava.description: The same complete runnable program in Java, in a single public class named Main with a main method. Same stdin format, same printed answer, same clearly marked stub.

stdinFormat.description: How one test case is laid out on standard input, described in one sentence so the harness and the tests agree.

testCases.description: Four cases. The first two must be the worked examples above. Include at least one edge case.

input.description: Written exactly as stdinFormat describes, ready to be piped into the program verbatim.

expected.description: Exactly what the program should print for that input, trimmed.
